q1.event_description: Coursera sits at the peak of online learning. ChatGPT doesn't exist yet. Enterprise is emerging as an opportunity. No major threats visible.

belief.prompt: What is your hypothesis about the consumer market over the next 8 quarters?

options.label: Stable & dominant. Consumer will remain our core.
Gradual shift. Some move to enterprise, but consumer stays significant.
Uncertain. Need more evidence before betting.

risks.prompt: What are the top risks you're taking with this allocation?

options.label: Consumer market disruption (new entrants, technology shift)
options.description: Real risk in online learning market

options.label: Instructor/talent attrition
options.description: Key creators may leave if not invested in

options.label: Enterprise sales cycles longer than expected
options.description: B2B adoption may be slower than forecast

options.label: Insufficient cash reserves
options.description: Spending too aggressively in early quarters

options.label: Technology capabilities falling behind
options.description: Not investing enough in product modernization

reflect.prompt: What did you learn from Q1?

options.label: Our strategy validated. We're on the right track.
Surprised by results. Need to adjust perspective.
Still unclear. Need more data.

role_hints.ceo: You are the CEO. You own the overall strategy and final decision. Are you confident in this allocation?
role_hints.cfo: You are the CFO. Cash is your concern. Will this allocation maintain healthy runway?
role_hints.product: You are the Chief Product Officer. Product quality and innovation are your domain. Is this investment in product/AI sufficient?
role_hints.people: You are the Chief People Officer. Instructor/talent satisfaction drives retention. Is this enough to keep creators happy?
role_hints.growth: You are the Chief Growth Officer. You own revenue and market expansion. Can this allocation drive the growth targets?

q2.event_description: OpenAI releases ChatGPT. Within weeks, it reaches 100M users. The market wakes up to generative AI as a real force. Consumer willingness to pay begins weakening. Enterprise suddenly sees opportunity in AI-enabled workforce learning.

belief.prompt: How do you interpret ChatGPT's arrival?

options.label: Noise. A cool tool, but not a threat to our business model.
Opportune. We can use AI to strengthen our position.
Threat. Students have free alternatives now. We need to respond urgently.
Mixed. Both threat and opportunity, unclear which dominates.

risks.prompt: What new risks emerge from ChatGPT?

options.label: Consumer churn to free AI alternatives
options.description: Students may cancel paid subscriptions

options.label: AI implementation delays our response
options.description: Building/integrating AI takes longer than expected

options.label: Culture shock from rapid change
options.description: Team overloaded by pace of disruption

options.label: Enterprise sales pause while they evaluate
options.description: Buyers wait to see what you do with AI

reflect.prompt: Based on Q2 evidence, how has your view of the market changed?

options.label: My belief from Q1 was confirmed. Proceeding as planned.
My Q1 belief was wrong. I need to change strategy.
Partial shift. Some adjustments, but staying mostly the course.
Still unclear. Need more evidence.

role_hints.ceo: The market has moved. Do we have the right strategy, or do we need to pivot?
role_hints.cfo: Cash is tight. We're spending on both old model and new. Can we sustain this?
role_hints.product: AI is now table stakes. Is our current product investment sufficient?
role_hints.people: Our team is stressed by rapid change. Culture may suffer. How do we support them?
role_hints.growth: Revenue is under pressure from consumer churn, but enterprise is waking up. Where is your growth focus?

q3.event_description: The market is consolidating post-ChatGPT shakeout. Weak competitors are fading. Instructors are choosing platforms. Enterprises are evaluating. Your Q1-Q2 choices now determine your market access and capability advantage.

belief.prompt: What is your core competitive advantage going into Q4?

options.label: Quality differentiation. Our content and instructors are the moat.
Enterprise integration. We're becoming the embedded learning platform.
AI innovation. Our AI capabilities are pulling ahead of competitors.
Diversified presence. We're winning across multiple segments.

risks.prompt: What worries you most about Q3 market shifts?

options.label: Consumer segment continuing to decline
options.description: Free AI alternatives are real threat

options.label: Enterprise sales cycles taking longer than expected
options.description: B2B decision-making is slow

options.label: Competitors leapfrogging us on AI
options.description: Venture-backed startups moving fast

options.label: Cash runway pressure from dual investment
options.description: Maintaining old model while building new

role_hints.ceo: Q3 reveals which of your Q1-Q2 bets are working. Are you prepared to make Q4 a true strategic choice, or are you hedging?
role_hints.cfo: Cash runway is your Q4 option generator. What options does current cash give us?
role_hints.product: Your capability stack from Q1-Q2 now determines what's possible in Q3-Q8. Can we fix weak areas, or do we live with what we built?
role_hints.people: Team is watching market moves closely. Uncertainty is growing. Q4 clarity will either energize or demoralize. Prepare them.
role_hints.growth: Market segments are differentiating. Volume consumer is under pressure. Enterprise and AI are the growth vectors. Where do you want to win?

q4.event_description: This is the pivot point. You choose your destination for Q5-Q8. This choice is irreversible. Your Q1-Q3 allocation and capabilities determine your readiness to execute. Choose wisely.

belief.prompt: Which destination best fits our company?

options.label: Consumer. Premium experience for individual learners.
Enterprise. Embedded learning platform for organizations.
AI-native. Pure-play AI learning engine.
Balanced. Diversified across all three segments.

risks.prompt: What is the biggest risk in your chosen destination?

options.label: We're not prepared for this destination
options.description: Q1-Q3 didn't build the right capabilities

options.label: Our team can't execute at this scale
options.description: Talent and culture constraints

options.label: Market shifts away from our chosen segment
options.description: Our bet on the wrong horse

options.label: Competitors dominate our chosen destination
options.description: We're not the market leader

role_hints.ceo: This is your call. Unit test your rationale: Can we execute this? Do we have the capabilities? Is this where we want to win?
role_hints.cfo: Cash runway determines Q4-Q8 survival. Conservative destination if cash tight. Aggressive destination if cash strong.
role_hints.product: Our product capabilities have been set by Q1-Q3 investment. This destination choice either leverages our strengths or exposes our weaknesses.
role_hints.people: Team unity on Q4 choice determines Q5-Q8 execution. Override their dissent and you risk execution failure during crunch times.
role_hints.growth: Your chosen destination determines your revenue model Q5-Q8. Growth rates, margins, and volatility all change based on this choice.

q5.event_description: Your Q4 destination choice meets the market for the first time. Is your strategy gaining traction? Do customers respond? Are your capabilities sufficient for execution?

belief.prompt: How is the market responding to your Q4 choice?

options.label: Stronger than expected. Early validation is clear.
As expected. Tracking to plan.
Weaker than expected. Market is skeptical.
Unclear. Too early to tell.
Our capabilities aren't ready to execute
options.description: We chose strategy we can't yet deliver

options.label: Market access is harder than expected
options.description: Customers take longer to commit

options.label: Competitors responded faster than expected
options.description: Market is already crowded

options.label: Cash burn faster than modeled
options.description: Q8 survival may require profitability sooner

role_hints.ceo: Q5 validation determines team morale. Strong signal energizes. Weak signal creates doubt. How do you communicate this result?
role_hints.cfo: Q5 revenue trajectory determines Q8 cash position. Early weakness means we need profitability by Q7.
role_hints.product: Q5 market response tests if your capabilities are truly differentiated. Execution gaps will be visible now.
role_hints.people: Q5 result impacts team confidence. Clear strategy validation (or refutation) affects culture and attrition risk.
role_hints.growth: Q5 determines if your Q4 destination has market demand. No validation = execution becomes much harder Q6-Q8.

q6.event_description: Q5 proved your strategy is real. Now competitors respond. Market gets crowded. Weak positions get crushed. Strong moats pay off. Can you defend your position?

belief.prompt: How do you defend your position against competitive attack?

options.label: Quality differentiation. Our product/experience is superior.
Switching costs. Our customers are locked in.
Price leadership. We out-compete on cost.
Segment migration. Move upmarket or into new segment.
We have no defensible moat
options.description: Competitors are feature-parity or better

options.label: Margin pressure from price competition
options.description: We must discount or lose share

options.label: Customer churn to competitors
options.description: Switching costs are lower than we thought

options.label: Talent drain to better-funded competitors
options.description: Our best people are leaving

role_hints.ceo: Q6 is your moat test. Do you have a defensible position? If not, Q7-Q8 are about survival, not growth.
role_hints.cfo: Competitive pressure means margin pressure. Can we sustain profitability while defending share?
role_hints.product: Competitive attack targets capability gaps. What's our sustainable competitive advantage?
role_hints.people: Team morale is under pressure from competitive intensity. Culture takes a hit Q6. How do we keep the team unified?
role_hints.growth: Q6 is about defending share or accepting decline. Growth is likely on hold. Focus is execution.

q7.event_description: Q6 competitive pressure is passing. But now Q7 asks: Can your organization actually scale? Execution and talent constraints become visible. This is the final test before Q8.

belief.prompt: Are we scaling our strategy successfully?

options.label: Scaling smoothly. Organization is keeping pace.
Hitting organizational limits. Friction is increasing.
Serious stress. Scaling is straining the organization.
Talent shortage. We cannot hire/retain what we need.
Culture damage from stress and uncertainty
options.description: Team morale is fragile

options.label: Technical debt limiting our ability to scale
options.description: System is creaking under load

options.label: Execution alignment issues (roles pulling different directions)
options.description: Team is not unified

options.label: Cash constraint limiting investments
options.description: We're out of runway to invest

role_hints.ceo: Q7 is your scaling test. Can the organization actually deliver Q4 strategy? Q8 will show if you chose the right destination AND could execute.
role_hints.cfo: Q7 is the final cash runway check. Q8 must be profitable or we die. Do we have runway to reach profitability?
role_hints.product: Q7 tests if your product can scale without quality degradation. Tech debt from Q1-Q6 now comes due.
role_hints.people: Q7 is crunch time. Team stress is maximum. Culture must hold or attrition spikes. Burnout is real risk.
role_hints.growth: Q7 is about execution, not growth. Revenue scaling depends on organizational capacity. Can we scale without breaking?

q8.event_description: Eight quarters complete. Your strategy revealed. Winners and losers clear. Now the retrospective: Did your choices lead to winning? Multidimensional scorecard: Financial + Strategic + Organizational. What did you learn?

belief.prompt: What does your Q1-Q8 journey teach you?

options.label: Strategy was right. Market validated our bet.
Strategy was wrong. Market rejected our destination.
Strategy was right but execution failed.
Our strategy worked but market luck helped.
Invest more in capability building Q1-Q3
options.description: Readiness matters

options.label: Invest more in culture and talent Q1-Q3
options.description: Execution requires healthy team

options.label: Choose different Q4 destination
options.description: This market wasn't right for us

options.label: Pivot earlier when strategy failed
options.description: Don't stay locked in failed destination

role_hints.ceo: Your Q4 destination choice cascaded through Q5-Q8. Early capability bets determined whether you were ready. Smart strategy + execution = winning.
role_hints.cfo: Cash management Q1-Q7 determined your Q8 options. Conservative burn enabled strategic optionality.
role_hints.product: Your Q1-Q3 capability investments are now your competitive advantage or disadvantage. No shortcuts.
role_hints.people: Your team's culture and execution alignment determined Q5-Q8 success. Happy, unified teams execute strategy. Fractured teams fail.
role_hints.growth: Q1-Q8 was about choosing where to compete and building the capabilities to win there. Growth came from coherence and execution, not luck.
